problem.title: Two Prime-Tile Trays
problem.statement: The prime inventories are 24 = 2³ × 3 and 36 = 2² × 3². What are the greatest product both inventories can supply and the least product containing enough prime copies to build either number?
hints: For the shared product, use the shorter stack in each prime column.
For the sufficient product, use the taller stack.

validationMethods: coordinate-wise minimum and maximum exponent calculation
independent divisibility checks 12 divides both and both divide 72
notes: The two inventory roles uniquely give 12 and 72.

problem.title: Shared Factors of Forty-Eight and Sixty
problem.statement: What is the greatest common divisor of 48 and 60?

notes: Twelve divides both inputs and no greater common factor exists.

problem.title: A Sufficient Multiple of Twelve and Eighteen
problem.statement: What is the least common multiple of 12 and 18?

validationMethods: independent ordered multiple lists first meeting at 36
notes: Thirty-six is divisible by both inputs and is their first positive common multiple.

problem.title: Both Trays from One Pair
problem.statement: What are the GCD and LCM, respectively, of 45 and 60?
hints: Build minimum and maximum exponent products separately.

solutionSteps.title: Build both products
solutionSteps.body: Minimum exponents give 3 × 5 = 15. Maximum exponents give 2² × 3² × 5 = 180.

validationMethods: coordinate-wise prime exponent minima and maxima
independent checks 15 divides both and both divide 180
product identity check 15 times 180 equals 45 times 60
notes: Choice B preserves operation order and both values.

problem.title: Signals Align Again
problem.statement: Two signals flash together now. One flashes every 8 minutes and the other every 12 minutes. After how many minutes will they first flash together again?
hints: The meeting time contains a whole number of both cycles.

solutionSteps.title: List the cycles
solutionSteps.body: Multiples of 8 are 8, 16, 24, … and multiples of 12 are 12, 24, …. The first positive match is 24.

validationMethods: independent prime calculation LCM of 2 cubed and 2 squared times 3 equals 24
notes: Twenty-four minutes is the first positive simultaneous time.

problem.title: First Common Multiple Past One Hundred
problem.statement: What is the least integer greater than 100 that is divisible by both 18 and 24?

solutionSteps.title: Apply the boundary
solutionSteps.body: The common multiples begin 72, 144, 216. The first greater than 100 is 144.

validationMethods: direct divisibility checks 144 divided by 18 is 8 and by 24 is 6
notes: The strict greater-than condition excludes 72 and selects 144.
